video_title: This Miami Heat Team Just Can't Beat the 76ers | Rachel Nichols & Chris Mannix

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Miami Heat's roster challenges after acquiring Giannis Antetokounmpo
quotes.excerpt: They gutted their team to get him, left a whole bunch of holes.
quotes.quote: The Miami Heat are in a tough position right now. They get Giannis Antetokounmpo, everybody is celebrating as they should. They hunted the big fish, they got him, gutted their team to get him, left a whole bunch of holes. Pat Riley said we need a playmaker. LeBron James was the best playmaker that is out there. Now LeBron is gone, and they are left with a big hole for a playmaker. They are left with big holes for perimeter shooters. They are still kind of in the mix. You see DeMar DeRozan talk out there, I am not sure what problems that he would ultimately solve. Maybe Clay Thompson gets bought out. Now we are doing the buyout thing where guys get bought out. It is like, wow, we got DeMar DeRozan at $3 million, we got Clay Thompson at $4 million. There is always a reason these guys are available and very rarely is it that they make a measurable difference.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: Local media influence on LeBron James' free agency decisions
quotes.excerpt: In the two cities of Cleveland and Miami, both cities were absolutely convinced they were getting LeBron.

text_blocks.speaker: Rachel Nichols
text_blocks.text: I don't blame them for wanting to be in the chase, and it's not their fault that a lot of the myth-making around both them and in Cleveland. It was really interesting over the three-plus weeks that LeBron was taking his time to make this decision. In the two cities of Cleveland and Miami, if you talk to people in those cities, both cities were absolutely convinced they were getting LeBron. And not in any way every local media radio person was contributing to this, but in both cities a lot of local media, not national but local media, was contributing to this. And not even local media, but just the local internet celebrities and everything. It was, I heard such and such, source tells me such and such. And I would see these reports and I was just like, man, you don't have better sources than the GM of the Miami Heat.

text_blocks.speaker: Rachel Nichols
text_blocks.text: And I was just like, man, you don't have better sources than the GM of the Miami Heat. Like, the general manager of the Miami Heat doesn't know. Your sources aren't better than his, right? The team officials you and I were talking to would flat out say, yeah, we don't know. So how would the third-hour radio guy know? I think the fans were done a disservice by some of the people in those markets who got them all worked up that they were getting that.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: Miami Heat's roster limitations and the difficulty of building a championship team

text_blocks.speaker: Rachel Nichols
text_blocks.text: What was available to the Heat was keeping the status quo, which was basically being a play-in team with not exciting players, middling draft picks, and an uncertain future. It requires so many different hitches to get to a team that becomes, oh, that's a great team. Yes, it requires LeBron James signing for $4 million. It requires Stephen Curry's ankles being shot and therefore signing at a discount, and then having a ballooned cap because of a TV deal and getting Kevin Durant. It takes Jaylen Brown to be coming over, only one team really believing he could be as good as he turned out to be, and then taking less money than he could have taken, and then getting Karl-Anthony Towns the way you did because Alex Rodriguez's group didn't want to pay as much for him. It takes a lot to get one of those teams where you can look at them and say at every position they're really the team they should be.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: You said middling draft picks. We don't know what they they what they might be down the line.

text_blocks.speaker: Rachel Nichols
text_blocks.text: We don't. But this is not a tanking team, and there aren't even supposed to be tanking teams anymore. So by definition, everything has to be kind of considered a middling draft pick unless you are just absolutely terrible and awful for two or three years, in which case that's got its own problems.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: The importance of the fan experience in an entertainment-driven NBA
quotes.excerpt: The fan experience is important. This is an entertainment league.
quotes.quote: The fan experience is important. This is an entertainment league. And so if you are going to go pay good money to watch your basketball team and they are not going to win a title, and I can tell you the Miami Heat in the old version were not going to win a title, and I would be surprised if in this version with Giannis Antetokounmpo, again, they could make changes and then I could say, oh my god, they're the favorite for the title. This version that we have right now, this roster, does not appear to me to be a favorite for the title. I'd rather see, if I have those two choices, I'd rather see the version with Giannis than 6-7-8 with Tyler Herro and a maybe future middling draft pick.
